messages.content: Help me execute a callback function named 'processResult' that handles an error 'null' and a result value of 'Operation successful'?

function.name: invokeCallback
function.description: This function invokes a callback with an error and a value. If the callback throws an error, it is caught and re-thrown asynchronously. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

callback.description: The callback function to be invoked. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

error.description: The error to pass to the callback function. Can be 'null' if there is no error. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

value.description: The value to pass to the callback function. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

The value is a string. According to the tool signature, callback is a string representation of a JavaScript object. So we should pass the function name as a string? It says "The callback function to be invoked. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation." So we can pass "processResult" as a string. The error: "null" as string? Or actual null? It says "Can be 'null' if there is no error. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation." So we can pass "null". The value: "'Operation successful'"? Should be string representation of the value. So we can pass "'Operation successful'" or "Operation successful"? Probably we need to pass the string representation of the value. So we can pass "'Operation successful'" (including quotes). But maybe we should pass "\"Operation successful\"" to represent a string. The tool expects JSON values. In JSON, strings are quoted. So we need to pass the string "Operation successful" as a JSON string. So the value field should be "Operation successful". The error field should be null (not string). But the spec says "Can be 'null' if there is no error. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation." So we can pass "null" as a string? But it's ambiguous. Let's interpret that we should pass the literal null value. So error: null. The callback: "processResult" as a string. The value: "Operation successful" as a string.

Thus we call:

{
  "callback": "processResult",
  "error": null,
  "value": "Operation successful"
}
